title: Pentecostalism worldwide
hook: from a plain mission on Azusa Street to Pentecostal churches across Africa, Asia and Latin America

segments.voice: Yesterday, abuse and the churches, a wound inside the house, and the millstone Jesus spoke of. Your line was believe them. Did you listen all the way through? Day nine hundred seventy-five.

No stained glass. No steeple. No pews. On Azusa Street in Los Angeles, a plain wooden building, once used as a stable and a storeroom, has sawdust on the floor and planks laid across barrels for benches. At the front, a preacher named William Seymour, the son of formerly enslaved parents, with a pair of wooden crates for a pulpit. In the room, Black and white and Latino worshipers, washerwomen and businessmen, side by side, in a city and a country that kept them apart. People pray out loud, weep, sing, and some speak in tongues. Today, what started in rooms like that one.

Pentecostalism takes its name from Pentecost, the day in Acts when the Holy Spirit comes on Jesus's followers in Jerusalem. In the King James Bible: "And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance." Then Peter stands up and quotes the prophet Joel: "I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy." All flesh. Sons and daughters. Pentecostals read that as a promise for now, not only for then. Speaking in tongues, prophecy, prayer for healing: the gifts of the Spirit, they say, are for ordinary believers today. And it showed in who led. At Azusa Street, women preached, and Black and white Christians laid hands on one another, which shocked plenty of observers. One early participant wrote, in effect, that the color line had been washed away. It didn't stay washed; Pentecostal churches later split along racial lines too, and that's part of the story. And some historians say the movement didn't spread from one center like spokes from a hub. They point to revivals with similar marks around the same era in India, Korea, Chile and parts of Africa, many led by local preachers rather than visiting missionaries. Today Pentecostal and charismatic churches are found from Lagos to Seoul to São Paulo, and charismatic renewal has reached Catholic and older Protestant churches too. Christians differ here. Pentecostals say the gifts continue. Some other Christians hold that certain gifts, like tongues, belonged to the apostles' time. Both read the same chapter of Acts.

Here's the practice: get to know a Pentecostal church, even from a distance. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind any Pentecostal or charismatic church you've passed: a rented room above a shop, a big hall by the highway, a congregation that meets in a school gym on Sundays. Picture the people walking in, the music starting, someone raising their hands. Let yourself be curious rather than wary. If you pray, you can pray for that congregation. Later, if you like, look up one near you, or ask a Pentecostal friend what Sunday is like. The bell holds the time.
Pentecostalism worldwide. A movement that reads Pentecost as a promise for today, with gifts of the Spirit for ordinary believers, now found across Africa, Asia and Latin America.
Your line: the spirit on all flesh. Today, take seriously one person whose voice usually gets skipped, and let them finish. Day nine hundred seventy-five.

howItsDone: Pentecostal worship is often loud and expressive, with long sung praise, raised hands, spontaneous prayer, prayer for healing, and speaking in tongues. Charismatic groups in Catholic and other churches pray in similar ways within their own traditions.

notes: Claims rule: the index's 'hundreds of millions today' is left out; no counts or dates. 'Found from Lagos to Seoul to São Paulo' is a non-numeric description.
Azusa Street mission details (former stable/storeroom, sawdust, planks on barrels, wooden crates as pulpit): commonly reported; confirm.
Seymour as the son of formerly enslaved parents: confirm.
'One early participant wrote, in effect, that the color line had been washed away' paraphrases Frank Bartleman ('the color line was washed away in the blood'); confirm attribution.
Later racial splits among Pentecostals: confirm general wording.
Independent revivals in India (e.g. the Mukti revival), Korea, Chile and Africa 'around the same era': confirm or soften.
Cessationist view described as 'some other Christians hold that certain gifts... belonged to the apostles' time'; confirm fair and unranked.
The screen head 'PENTECOST: TONGUES OF FIRE' draws on Acts 2:3 (cloven tongues like as of fire); the voice quotes 2:4. Confirm acceptable.
